messages:
tasha: FYI - ACME Health's security team rejected PrivateLink for the POC. They only allow VPC peering with strict ACLs. Need a concise peering runbook we can hand to their infra team and any caveats for routing and key delivery. POC target: 10 days.

ben: Understood. High-level peering runbook: 1) Confirm non-overlapping CIDRs. 2) Create VPC peering from their account -> our shared-peering account. 3) Accept peering on our side. 4) Update route tables in both VPCs to point to the peering attachment for the specific subnets. 5) Update security groups to allow 443 from the peer CIDRs. 6) If they use NACLs, open ephemeral ports for return traffic (1024-65535). 7) Validate with curl from a jump host in their VPC to our control-plane IP.

omar: A few gotchas from networking: - Overlapping CIDRs is a deal blocker, we can't peer if ranges overlap. - Propagation: make sure they don't rely solely on propagated routes; explicitly add routes for the subnets used by our endpoints. - AZs don't matter for peering, but ensure the subnets you intend to hit have route entries. - If they use AWS Transit Gateway, peering may be disallowed or require TGW attachments instead. - DNS: peering does not provide private DNS mapping. We'll provide an internal IP or they must use public DNS (so traffic goes via NAT).

ben: About API keys and control plane access if peering only: options: A) Public control plane with IP allowlist: we can provide a small set of egress IPs for them to NAT through; they must NAT traffic to those IPs and we allowlist. B) Run a customer-side proxy in their VPC that forwards to our hosted API over the internet (not ideal). C) Offer a short-term Dedicated pool or Private deployment for the POC so traffic stays inside private interconnects. Note: IP allowlisting requires static egress IPs on their side (NAT GW or egress NAT instances).

mira: Security asked about key exchange method if we can't use PrivateLink. They don't want to paste keys in email.

ben: We can provision a scoped POC API key with a 48-hour TTL and push it into their secret manager via a signed, short-lived presigned upload link or share via a vault (1Password/Bitwarden) integration. Audit recorded. We log key issuance in our internal audit service with an audit-id. CloudTrail will capture peering accept events.

omar: For the route table TF snippet (customer side) - minimal example to add a route for our control-plane subnet through the peering attachment:
```
resource "aws_vpc_peering_connection" "peer_redwood" {
  provider = aws.customer
  vpc_id = var.customer_vpc_id
  peer_vpc_id = var.redwood_vpc_id
  peer_owner_id = var.redwood_account_id
  peer_region = var.redwood_region
}

resource "aws_vpc_peering_connection_accepter" "accept" {
  provider = aws.redwood
  vpc_peering_connection_id = aws_vpc_peering_connection.peer_redwood.id
  auto_accept = true
}

resource "aws_route" "to_redwood" {
  route_table_id = var.customer_route_table_id
  destination_cidr_block = var.redwood_service_cidr
  vpc_peering_connection_id = aws_vpc_peering_connection.peer_redwood.id
}
```
Replace vars with real IDs. They must also add reciprocal routes in our route tables.

ben: Testing checklist for customer infra: - Confirm peering status = active on both accounts. - From a bastion in their app subnet: `curl -v https://<control-plane-public-host>/health` should return 200 (if using NAT/IP allowlist) or test against our provided internal IP if we've coordinated. - If TLS name mismatch, ensure they hit the DNS name that matches our cert. - If 403, check SG and route.

mira: Does our side need to change any security group to allow CIDR ranges? We prefer locking to specific subnets rather than whole VPC.

omar: Yes, recommend locking to the exact /24 or narrower CIDRs they provide for the app subnets. Security groups are stateful; allow inbound 443 from those CIDRs. Avoid 0.0.0.0/0.

deploy-bot: Ticket POC-6031 created: "ACME peering POC - peering + key delivery". Owner: ben. SLA: 2 business days to accept peering.

ben: I'll set our acceptance to manual so we can verify CIDRs before accepting. After acceptance we'll add route table entries and update SGs. I'll also create a short-lived key and flag audit-id in the ticket.

mira: Great. I'll send the runbook to their infra with the TF snippet and the three testing commands. If they push back on NAT/allowlist, open the Dedicated/Private option in the SOW.

tasha: Thanks team. I'll update the timeline with the 2-day acceptance window and add a note that PrivateLink would have been simpler for DNS and no-route changes.

ben: One more note: if they later want to switch to PrivateLink, we'll need to unpeer or add explicit routes to prefer PrivateLink DNS; plan for a short cutover window to avoid blackholing traffic.

mira: Copy. Closing loop for now, will report back after their infra replies with CIDRs and peering request ID.
